howItWorks.heading: Three steps, at your own pace
howItWorks.lead: These steps all happen in the LifePoem mobile app, on your phone or tablet.

steps.title: Tell a memory
steps.body: Speak or type about a moment from your life.
steps.aside: Hold the large record button while you talk, or use the keyboard if you prefer.

steps.title: Let the story unfold
steps.body: Gentle questions help you recall the people, places, and feelings.
steps.aside: One question at a time, and you answer in your own words. Nothing is timed.

steps.title: Keep it. Share it.
steps.body: Turn your memories into a written story for yourself and your family.
steps.aside: Stories are saved on your device, and sync to your account once you sign in and reconnect.

pace.heading: No writing skill required. Nothing to rush.
pace.body: LifePoem was built with older adults, so the things that usually get in the way — small text, hidden buttons, forms that hurry you — are not part of it.
pace.offlineBody: your stories are saved on your device, and sync to your account once you sign in and reconnect. Voice transcription and story writing need an internet connection.

features.title: Speak or type
features.body: Hold to record your voice, or write with the keyboard. Both work the same way.

features.title: Large text and clear controls
features.body: Big buttons and adjustable reading sizes, so you can set what is comfortable.

features.title: Read-aloud replies
features.body: Listen to the questions and your finished story instead of reading them.

features.title: Four familiar languages
features.body: English, 中文, Bahasa Melayu and தமிழ் — in the app and on this website.

features.title: Gentle prompts, without pressure
features.body: Questions arrive one at a time. Stop and come back whenever you want.

example.heading: The things only you remember
example.bodyOne: A kitchen at six in the morning. The first pay packet. Advice from a grandmother that still holds. These are the details families ask about later, and the ones easiest to leave unsaid.
example.bodyTwo: A finished story can take three shapes, so it sounds the way the memory feels.

prose.definition: reads like a short chapter from a memoir.

diary.definition: dated and close to the moment, in your own voice.

example.footnote: Written from a short spoken memory. Example text created for this design, not a customer story.

prose.title: The Kitchen at Six in the Morning
paragraphs: My mother was always awake before the rest of us. By the time I came down the stairs the kettle had already boiled twice, the rice was on, and the window above the sink had gone soft with steam. She never said good morning. She would push a bowl across the table towards me and carry on with whatever her hands were doing.

Years later I understood that this was how she said the things she never said out loud. A bowl pushed across a table, still too hot to hold. I have made that same breakfast for my own children, in a different kitchen, in a different country, and every time I set the bowl down I hear the kettle in that first house.

diary.title: Steam on the window
paragraphs: Up before six again. The kitchen is the only room that is warm at this hour, so I sit with my hands around the cup and let the window fog over. Outside, the neighbour's bicycle is already gone.

I thought about my mother today, and how she never once wished me a good morning. It did not occur to me until this year that she was saying it the whole time, with the rice, with the bowl, with the door left unlocked for me.

You asked me once what my mother was like and I do not think I answered you properly. She was not a woman who said very much. She was awake before anyone else in the house, every day of her life, and the kitchen window was always steamed over by the time I came downstairs.

She would push a bowl of rice across the table to me and say nothing at all. I want you to know that this was affection, and that I recognised it, even then. When I make that breakfast for you, that is what I am doing too.

contact.metaDescription: Reach the LifePoem team for help with the app, getting started, or support for a family member.
contact.heading: We are glad to help
contact.lead: Tell us what you need — a question about the app, trouble getting started, or help for a family member. A person reads every message.
contact.nameHelp: However you like to be addressed.
contact.emailHelp: So we can reply to you.
contact.emailError: Please enter an email address like name@example.com.
contact.messageHelp: At least 10 characters. Tell us what is happening and which phone you use, if that helps.
contact.privacyLine: We use your name, email and message only to answer you. Nothing is stored on this website.
contact.invalidMessage: Something went wrong. Please check your details and try again.
contact.failureMessage: We could not pass your message to our email provider just now.
contact.failureFallback: You can also email us at support@lifepoem.one and we will pick it up from there.
contact.successBody: Your message has been accepted by our email provider and is on its way to the support mailbox. If you do not hear back, write to support@lifepoem.one directly.
contact.asideDirectBody: If the form gives you trouble, email support@lifepoem.one from your own mail app.
contact.asideDeleteBody: The steps are written out on the {link} page.
